body: Owner is exploring a macOS VM for hands-off live checks. Host: M4 Pro, 14 cores, 24 GB, 816 GB free, macOS 26.5.1; Parallels 20.4.1 Standard, perpetual (caps 4 vCPU, 8 GB). The owner created VM "macOS" through Parallels' free macOS download: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) restore image (19.8 GB IPSW in ~/Downloads, served by Apple's CDN), 4 vCPU, 6 GB, 128 GiB sparse disk (24 GB used mid-install), shared network, 3D highest, shared clipboard/cloud/applications on. Research (cited) found: host-only networking is supported for macOS guests on Parallels 20.4+ with host 15+; clipboard is unsupported for macOS guests; snapshots are supported from PD 20; the CLI is officially Pro-only; Parallels pairs macOS 26 with PD 26 (older versions not fully compatible); free fallback UTM (Apache-2.0) on the same IPSW; the macOS SLA 2B(iii) allows two VM copies for development and testing. That guest-posted events stay in the guest is architecturally expected but undocumented; to be proven on first run with the host's listen-only guard.
